//: Hold out in a house on the lane through one night (13 §11, a survival game in small). The game begins at ten at night in front of a house. Three strangers come for the character down the lane, not at once: the first is on the lane already, the second comes from the east at half past eleven and the third at one in the morning (`core:last_stand_stranger`, run from `start.do` and from two timers). Each is a person who thinks with the `guard` mind (09 §3.1) and perceives with its senses, given when the mind's state is first made (decision D-901), with a knife in hand; each is tagged `hostile` and holds the character hostile, and the house is each one's beat, so that they walk the lane before its door and come for the character once they see it; and the character, who was told they mean harm, holds each of them hostile in turn (so walking into one strikes, and a long wait is broken off when one comes into sight). `start.do` marks the nearest door as the refuge and lights a lamp beside it, the one light on a dark lane, which a player may leave burning to see them come or put out to hide; leaves a club and two bandages on the table inside, something to fight with for whoever has nothing and something to bind wounds with, a lamp in the room to find them by (which may be switched off, to hide), and a wardrobe against a wall further in, to hide in; and sets a timer for dawn, seven hours on, at five, when the sky begins to lighten (the calendar's dawn), that completes the objective of holding out. The player chooses who they are among the playable templates, ready-made (13 §4.2), or is an ordinary person. Getting inside comes first. The game ends when dawn comes or when the character dies, and it has one save, gone when it ends. A stranger who loses sight of the character where there is somewhere to hide searches the house (`core:search_hiding_places`, decision D-950): its rooms as the light lets him see, and the wardrobe, which he opens; one who never perceived her go in does not. Tuned by play-testing (decisions D-909, D-950).
name: Last stand
doc: A house on the lane at night, and strangers on the road. Hold out until dawn.
intro: It is ten at night. Three strangers are coming down the lane, one by one, and they mean you harm. Get into the house and hold out until dawn, at five.

cells.where: not it.under_open_sky and it.standable and (it.fixture.def_id ?? 'engine:none') == 'engine:none' and (dist(it, $door) ?? 0) > 2.5
it.z == $door.z and not it.under_open_sky and it.standable and (it.fixture.def_id ?? 'engine:none') == 'engine:none' and (dist(it, $door) ?? 0) > 2.9

doc: One of the last stand's strangers comes (`core:last_stand`): a person who thinks as a watchman (`guard`) is made at `at`, given a knife in hand, tagged `hostile`, holds `self` (the character) hostile and is held so in turn, and has the house before which the game began as its beat (`global.var.stand_home`); what it knows of the character it perceives, and it searches the house for her once it has lost her there (decision D-950).

name: the strangers
doc: The last stand's strangers (`core:last_stand`): they tell each other what they perceive of the one they came for, and whoever comes later is told on coming (15 §9.2).

if: self.in_group('core:strangers') and not is_null(about) and self.hostile(about)
doc: One of the last stand's strangers who comes to perceive someone he holds hostile tells the others where (`report_to_group`): what he perceived, as told, and to whoever comes after (decision D-962).

if: self.in_group('core:strangers') and not is_null(about) and self.hostile(about)
doc: One of the last stand's strangers who loses someone he holds hostile tells the others where he last perceived them (decision D-962).
The door of the house the character holds out in (`core:last_stand`).
Where the last stand's strangers walk their beat: the lamp before the house's door, else the door (`core:last_stand`).
